summary: The Virginia Graeme Baker Pool and Spa Safety Reauthorization Act reauthorizes and updates federal swimming pool and spa safety grant programs and public education efforts through fiscal year 2030. It expands eligible grant recipients to include certain nonprofit organizations alongside states and Indian tribes, sets specific funding rules and priorities for grant distribution, creates internal staff positions at the Consumer Product Safety Commission, and mandates reporting and awareness campaigns.

affected_groups.effect: May apply for federal grants to fund pool safety enforcement, inspections, and public education campaigns.
affected_groups.group: States, Indian Tribes, and Nonprofit Organizations

affected_groups.effect: Must manage the grant program, carry out public education campaigns, hire a Director of Drowning Prevention, conduct outreach, and report annually to Congress.
May receive targeted grant services and educational materials aimed at addressing drowning disparities.

key_provisions: Expands the definition of covered entities eligible for pool safety grants to include states, Indian tribes, and qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations with drowning prevention experience.

Requires states and Indian tribes receiving grants to use at least 25 percent of funds for personnel to enforce safety standards and inspect or repair drain covers, and the remainder for public education.
Sets priorities for grant awards, favoring first-time recipients, expansion of existing educational activities, areas with high per-capita drowning rates, and underserved or rural communities.
Establishes a Director of Drowning Prevention and requires more than one full-time equivalent staff member dedicated to these activities at the Consumer Product Safety Commission.

Authorizes $2,500,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 for the swimming pool safety grant program, and another $2,500,000 annually for the same period for a public education and awareness program.

Requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission to conduct a grant awareness campaign, report annually to Congress on the grant program, and develop educational materials targeting disadvantaged communities with higher-than-average drowning rates.
